summary: Cool, quiet Friday in Berthoud. The biggest signal today: Nvidia’s founder resigns four days before earnings.

verse.text: For this is the will of God, that by doing good you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men, as free, yet not using liberty as a cloak for vice, but as bondservants of God.

devotional.title: Sailing Through the Tempest

scripture.text: We went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.

devotional.body: Paradoxical though it be, only that man is at rest who attains it through conflict. This peace, born of conflict, is not like the deadly hush preceding the tempest, but the serene and pure-aired quiet that follows it.
devotional.attribution: L. B. Cowman, Streams in the Desert (1925)

top_signals.headline: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigns as CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim. Earnings Nov. 17.
Microsoft 365 outage recovering after a global failure; some users may still see delays.
Brooklyn collapse becomes a criminal inquiry after the search for victims ends.

sectors.title: AI and Tech
sectors.summary: Nvidia loses its founder four days before earnings, Microsoft 365 is still recovering, and Anthropic’s listing is expected Nov. 17.

items.title: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigns
items.brief: CEO and board member after 33 years; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
items.detail: Earnings are due Nov. 17 and House chairs want a closed-door briefing. Reports of probes and congressional letters are not settled findings.

items.title: Microsoft 365 recovering from global outage
items.brief: Outlook and Teams disruptions ran into Friday; email queues approaching normal.
items.detail: Microsoft says servers failed automated health checks, pushing traffic onto remaining systems and overloading them, and that it found no malicious activity. NHS England, courts and city offices were among those affected.

items.title: Anthropic listing expected Nov. 17
items.brief: Trading is expected to begin the same day as Nvidia earnings.
items.detail: The listing follows a sharp AI-stock sell-off that lowered valuation estimates.

items.title: Google AI glasses open for pre-order
items.brief: Gemini-powered glasses with Samsung start at $395 and ship Dec. 10.
items.detail: They have no in-lens display and blur bystanders’ faces before Gemini sees them.

items.title: FBI ties $400 million scam to North Korea
items.brief: Fake video calls in a scheme called FaceStealer hit more than 900 victims.
items.detail: The bureau says the scheme ran over 18 months.

items.title: Waymo fix under federal review
items.brief: NHTSA is examining Waymo’s school-bus safety fix.
items.detail: The company reportedly plans 20,000 vehicles by late 2027.

sectors.title: Berthoud and Northern Colorado
sectors.summary: A bridge closure starts Monday near Platteville, the Front Range rail tax passes, and one contested wildlife vote heads to January.

items.title: WCR 31 bridge closure starts Monday
items.brief: Weld County Road 31 closes between roads 36 and 38 on Nov. 16.
items.detail: Crews will replace a 53-year-old bridge near Platteville and Gilcrest. Work is scheduled through March 5, 2027.

items.title: Rail tax passes, district plans buildout
items.brief: Ballot Issue 7A passing 56% to 44% in unofficial returns.
items.detail: The permanent 0.333% sales tax funds Front Range passenger rail. Starter service would run three round trips a day between Denver and Fort Collins, stopping in Loveland and Longmont.

items.title: Prairie dog shooting ban advances
items.brief: Colorado Parks and Wildlife voted 6-5 to send a petition to a January vote.
items.detail: The petition would ban recreational prairie dog shooting on public land, including the Pawnee National Grassland. Supporters call it needless; opponents say the process moved too fast. It would not affect private land.

items.title: Hoedown Hill drops skiing
items.brief: The Windsor venue will focus on live music and outdoor entertainment this winter.
items.detail: The venue was known for skiing, snowboarding and tubing.

items.title: Downtown parking ribbon-cutting Wednesday
items.brief: Windsor marks completion of its parking project at 1:15 p.m. Nov. 18.
items.detail: The site is at 107 5th St., between Main Street and Boardwalk Park. Work replaced an aging waterline, added a sewer line and built a lot.

sectors.title: U.S. News and Politics
sectors.summary: The Brooklyn collapse is now a criminal case, a polar vortex reversal could chill Thanksgiving week, and Senate Democrats face a leadership challenge.

items.title: Criminal inquiry into Brooklyn collapse
items.brief: Prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into the Flatbush collapse that killed eight.
items.detail: City inspectors are examining whether excavation at the neighboring construction site caused it and are reviewing about 100 other sites tied to the five entities involved.

items.title: Earliest polar vortex reversal on record
items.brief: Arctic winds reversed on Nov. 10, the earliest in records back to 1958.
items.detail: Forecasters say it may favor colder air in parts of the U.S. around Thanksgiving, though the effect on winter weather is uncertain.

items.title: Van Hollen challenges Schumer
items.brief: The Maryland senator will run for Democratic leader; Sanders backs him.
items.detail: Schumer says he has the votes. A secret-ballot caucus vote is expected in early December.

items.title: Alito warns on court funding
items.brief: Congress could “turn off the lights” at the Supreme Court by cutting funds.
items.detail: He spoke at the Federalist Society dinner and called judicial independence essential.

items.title: Bessent faults Commerce over Megaspeed
items.brief: Treasury, Pentagon and State favored an Entity List addition for months.
items.detail: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify to the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10. Commerce did not comment to CBS.

items.title: Shutdown risk over Pentagon money
items.brief: Some GOP senators warn the budget process could threaten funding talks.
items.detail: The warning concerns how Pentagon funding moves through the process.

sectors.title: World and Conflict
sectors.summary: Strikes and counterclaims continue in Ukraine, Iran and Yemen, and the IAEA says it still cannot inspect a declared Iranian plant.

items.title: Second car bomb in Russia in two days
items.brief: A remote bomb critically injured former Azarov adviser Sergei Zavorotnyi in Moscow.
items.detail: A day earlier a bomb killed a serviceman in St. Petersburg. Moscow blames Kyiv; Ukraine has not commented.

items.title: Record drone exchange
items.brief: Russia says it downed 1,198 Ukrainian drones; it launched 117 at Ukraine.
items.detail: Refineries were hit, and a Kyiv hospital was struck. Both sides report deaths.

items.title: Iran claims Bahrain radar strike
items.brief: The IRGC says it destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar; CENTCOM says it did not.
items.detail: CENTCOM says both drones launched were shot down, with no injuries or damage.

items.title: IAEA “increasingly concerned” over Isfahan
items.brief: It has never inspected an enrichment plant Iran declared in June 2025.
items.detail: The watchdog does not know the plant’s exact location or whether it holds nuclear material. Iran says monitoring cannot proceed while it is under threat.

items.title: ANC posts worst result ever
items.brief: About 31% in local elections, down from 46% in 2021.
items.detail: The party lost majorities in Johannesburg, Pretoria and Ekurhuleni. Coalition talks follow.

items.title: COP31 split on final text
items.brief: Turkey and Australia issued a wish list including a 35% electrification target by 2035.
items.detail: Nations remain divided on fossil fuels and finance.

sectors.title: Notes
sectors.summary: Headlines from The Worldview and one idea from The Diary Of A CEO.

items.title: Persecution with a good ending
items.brief: Titus fled Sudan as a refugee to Kenya and has now earned a college degree.
items.detail: The Worldview in 5 Minutes credits International Christian Concern, which has helped him since 2023. He credits Jesus as his shelter through the journey.

items.title: “Not Dead Yet”
items.brief: Former Sen. Ben Sasse, facing pancreatic cancer, launched a podcast on gratitude.
items.detail: The podcast is with Chris Stirewalt and focuses on living with gratitude and purpose.

items.title: Habits and the brain
items.brief: How sleep, exercise, blood sugar and social connection may affect dementia risk.
items.detail: The neurologist also discusses inflammation and alcohol.
